DEFAULT_BIND is now 0.0.0.0:9443, with the reason in a doc comment and in asterius.example.toml. README's getting-started URL follows. Config test asserts the default. 9443 verified free on the dev host.

axum + rustls bootstrap in both modes. TLS: 1.2/1.3 only, nine BCP 195 suites named explicitly, ALPN h2+http/1.1; real openssl s_client handshake tests prove 1.0/1.1 refused, 1.2/1.3 accepted, negotiated suite ECDHE+AEAD, and that the TLS port answers nothing in cleartext. Middleware: security headers (HSTS 31536000 includeSubDomains preload, nosniff, DENY, no-referrer, permissions-policy) outermost so they survive 404/408/413; CSPRNG request id, client-supplied one ignored; 64 KiB body limit (413); 10s timeout (408); 16 KiB header block (431). No CORS layer anywhere, asserted by a source audit plus a runtime test over OPTIONS/GET/POST on /authorize and /token with Origin. Redirects go through one SeeOther helper that can only emit 303 and rejects CR/LF in Location; a source audit fails the build on any other redirect status. behind_proxy mode believes forwarding headers only from configured CIDRs, walking the chain from the right. Swapped rustls-pemfile (RUSTSEC-2025-0134, unmaintained) for rustls-pki-types. 99 tests, 1.3s without a database.

Tenant = issuer, resolved before any handler runs. asterius_oidc::tenancy::route is pure and accepts both well-known forms (OIDC Discovery s4 path-appending and RFC 8414 s3.1 path-insertion), rejecting a path-insertion suffix that is not exactly a tenant. TenantId::parse admits only [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63} — no dot, no percent, no upper case — so traversal and encoding tricks are refused before the directory is consulted; config validates tenant ids too. The middleware verifies the host belongs to the resolved tenant (issuer authority or custom_host), so a tenant cannot be reached through a host it does not own; absent/disabled/wrong-host all return an identical 404. It rewrites the path, so handlers mount at /authorize and never see tenancy — applied via Router::fallback_service because Router::layer runs after routing. Behind a proxy, X-Forwarded-Host/Forwarded host is believed only from trusted CIDRs. TenantDirectory caches an immutable snapshot with explicit invalidate() plus a 30s TTL for other replicas; no Redis. Binary bootstraps configured tenants idempotently at startup. 143 tests, 1.9s. Deferred: the invalid_client half of the acceptance needs a client model — noted on ast-m9c.2.

Audit core: AuditEvent with actor + delegation chain (RFC 8693 act), subject/client/session/grant links (FAPI 2.0 SP s6.7 item 4), closed EventType vocabulary, AuditSink port. Redaction is two-layer: Detail values are typed so a credential can only enter as a SHA-256 fingerprint, and free text is scanned for JWT / Bearer+DPoP / PEM / >=128-bit opaque shapes and replaced before insert. Per-tenant SHA-256 hash chain over a length-prefixed canonical encoding (JSON would be forgeable by key order; unprefixed concatenation would let a field boundary move) — detects and locates both an edited row and a deleted one. Append-only enforced in the database: UPDATE always refused, DELETE only for the retention job, which announces itself with a transaction-local asterius.retention flag. Retention is idempotent and leaves the remaining chain verifiable from its new start. 173 tests, 1.1s without a database; 19 DB tests. Deferred: the real flow sequence assertion needs the PAR/authorize/token endpoints — the trail-ordering test stands in until then.

Redaction is a tracing field formatter (RedactingFields), not a call-site rule: every field of every event and span is scanned, whole values and credential-shaped runs embedded in larger strings — the acceptance test logs a whole code flow the careless way at TRACE and found three real holes (Debug dump of a response struct, positional message, error built by format!) that whole-value matching missed. Fields named like secrets are redacted regardless of shape; sub/username/email are hashed so lines stay correlatable. Shares the scanner with the audit trail so the two cannot drift. Prometheus metrics with closed low-cardinality label sets (endpoint route, grant type, OAuth error code, five status classes) plus a build_info gauge. /healthz never touches the database (a DB outage must not get every replica killed); /readyz pings it and reports 503 - verified live: 503 in 2.0s during a real outage, after a 2s probe timeout was added because sqlx otherwise waited out its acquire timeout and the probe hung. 188 tests.

cargo-fuzz harness with six targets over the parsers that exist today (issuer_parse, tenant_route, config_parse, redaction_scan, forwarded_resolve, audit_canonical). scripts/check-fuzz-coverage.sh enforces the DoD both ways: a '// fuzz-target: name' marker without a target fails, and a target nothing claims fails too (verified by deleting one). Wired into CI as a 60s-per-target smoke job gating the required CI check, plus fuzz-nightly.yml at 10min/target with a cached corpus. Targets assert invariants, not just absence of panic. All six clean: issuer_parse 2.4M, config_parse 1.34M, forwarded_resolve 1.6M, audit_canonical 693k, redaction_scan 621k, tenant_route 16.5M executions. Three findings: two were bugs in my own targets (str slicing at non-char boundaries), one was real — tenancy::route was not total, returning a non-path for empty input and passing relative segments through; it now rejects both, with tests. The three targets the bead names (form-urlencoded, JWT compact, JSON metadata) are owed when those parsers land; the coverage script will demand them automatically.

JOSE on aws-lc-rs (ADR-0004: josekit pulls OpenSSL, which deny.toml bans). SigningAlgorithm is a closed 3-variant enum in asterius-domain so asterius-oidc can publish it in metadata without depending on an adapter; none/HS256/RS256 are not representable. SigningKey generates/imports/exports PKCS#8 for EdDSA, ES256, PS256 with the FAPI 2.0 SP s5.4.1 RSA-2048 floor checked on both paths; public_jwk emits RFC 7517/7518 members and no private ones. JWS compact serialisation per RFC 7515 s7.1: verification uses the key's algorithm and requires the header to agree (RFC 8725 s3.1-3.2), signing covers the encoded bytes so a re-encoded header cannot reuse a signature, explicit typ required (s3.11), any crit refused. LocalKeyStore implements the KeyStore and Signer ports with RFC 7638 thumbprint kids - verified against the RFC's published test vector - and rotation that retires rather than replaces so pre-rotation tokens still verify. 28 jose tests including per-byte signature tampering across all three algorithms. jws_parse fuzz target registered; coverage gate at 7 parsers.

One verifier for every JWT the server accepts (client assertions, DPoP proofs, request objects, id_token_hint, CIBA, logout tokens). Policy has no Default - typ and the algorithm list are decisions a caller must make. Checks ordered so cost precedes trust: size before parsing, structure and crit, algorithm against the caller's list, signature against a resolver-chosen key, claims last. FAPI 2.0 SP s5.3.2.1 item 13 implemented exactly: iat/nbf 0-10s ahead accepted, >60s refused, and with_future_skew clamps rather than rejects so a misconfiguration yields a compliant server. exp has zero leeway; a string NumericDate is not a NumericDate. aud checked in both RFC 7519 s4.1.3 spellings. s5.4.3 duplicate-kid handling: candidates filtered by algorithm then each tried, with a test that puts the decoy first so passing cannot be an ordering accident. 8 KiB default size cap, configurable. jws::Header.kid became Optional because a DPoP proof carries jwk instead (RFC 9449 s4.2). 48 jose tests; jwt_verify fuzz target added, coverage gate at 8 parsers.

OpaqueToken::generate defaults to 256 bits, base64url unpadded; generate_bits::<BITS>() makes the 128-bit FAPI 2.0 SP s5.4.1 floor a compile error via a const assert rather than a Result. Secret<T> and OpaqueToken deliberately do not implement PartialEq, so == on them does not compile; secret_audit.rs asks the compiler whether the trait is still absent (inherent-vs-trait associated const) so a future #[derive(PartialEq)] fails the build, and greps for the one remaining exit, secret.expose() == candidate, folding continuation lines so rustfmt cannot split a comparison into two innocent halves. I verified BOTH mechanisms myself by injecting violations: the derive produces two independent errors, and the grep half located the injected expose() comparison by file and line. ct_eq via subtle for every secret comparison; sha256_hex for at-rest lookup. Statistical test is a collision check plus Pearson chi-square over the 64-symbol alphabet, counting only the 42 fully-determined 6-bit groups (the 43rd character carries 4 bits and would make a correct generator look skewed), ~1ms. No fuzz target: from_presented validates nothing by design, so no attacker-controlled bytes become a typed value. Implemented by a subagent in a worktree; merged with conflicts in Cargo.toml, domain lib.rs and the threat model resolved by hand.

Client aggregate + validating parser. Defaults are the FAPI values and anything weaker is rejected, never defaulted. Implemented by a subagent in a worktree; I merged it and then closed the schema gap it reported. Notable decisions: response_types is ['code'] or empty and nothing else, so a client_credentials client stays expressible (RFC 7591 s2.1); a non-canonical redirect URI is refused rather than rewritten, because url parses https:///cb into https://cb/ and storing raw bytes for byte-exact matching while a browser resolves something else is a real divergence; errors never echo the document, enforced by a property test; the repository re-validates on read so a row weakened by hand fails to load. I added the nine missing columns to the baseline migration (application_type, subject_type, sector_identifier_uri, the two optional signing algs, the token-binding pair, authorization_details_types, use_mtls_endpoint_aliases) plus two CHECK constraints - a client bound to neither DPoP nor a certificate cannot exist, and a sector_identifier_uri without a pairwise subject cannot exist - so upsert no longer has to refuse valid clients. 305 tests, all gates green.

One Endpoint registry in asterius-oidc::metadata is the only input to both the router and the discovery document, so an endpoint cannot be advertised without being routed or routed without being advertised - asserted in both directions. Endpoints whose stories have not landed are mounted with 501 handlers rather than omitted, because OIDC Discovery s3 makes authorization_endpoint/token_endpoint/jwks_uri REQUIRED and a document missing them is invalid, not smaller; 501 also tells a client 'right URL, not yet' where 404 would say 'wrong URL'. All four discovery URLs (OIDC and RFC 8414 names, path-appended and path-inserted) return byte-identical documents. Golden-file test pins the whole document. JWKS serves public members only (test greps for d/p/q/dp/dq/qi/k), never x5u/jku/x5c per FAPI 2.0 SP s5.4.2, no duplicate kid, cacheable with a body-derived ETag. Verified live: real Ed25519 JWKS and metadata from the running binary. 332 tests. Deferred to ast-mxc.3: JWKS max-age tied to rotation cadence (noted there).

One exact-comparison function used by registration, and by PAR (ast-gxh.1) and the token endpoint (ast-a05.2) when they land: RedirectUri::is_registered(registered, presented, application_type). Byte-exact per RFC 3986 s6.2.1; the RFC 8252 s7.3 loopback exception varies the port and nothing else. ADR-0005 records the decision to keep exact matching even though RFC 9126 s2.4 and RFC 9700 s4.1.3 permit relaxing it for PAR-pushed URIs. Implemented by a subagent, which mutation-tested its own work (three deliberate breakages, each caught, one found by the fuzzer in 45s). I then ran an independent 25-case adversarial probe of my own choosing - prefix/suffix, /a/../cb traversal, IDN homoglyph host, 127.0.0.1:51004@evil.example, :443 vs default, a web client attempting the loopback branch, empty registered set - all behaved correctly. Deliberate behaviour change: registration now dedupes with the real comparison, so two loopback entries differing only in port are one registration; otherwise MAX_REDIRECT_URIS could hold 32 port variants of one callback and the reviewed set would not be the effective set. 347 tests.

States pending/active/retiring/retired with a per-tenant schedule; private keys sealed with AES-GCM under a KEK from a Kek port (LocalKek for dev, async so a cloud KMS fits). Implemented by a subagent in a worktree. Verified independently: I read the stored bytes out of PostgreSQL and they are opaque (73d66d26..., not a DER SEQUENCE), nonce is 96 bits, length is PKCS#8 + 16-byte GCM tag, kek_id is derived, and a rotation leaves active+pending which is publish-before-sign. Notable: RandomizedNonceKey means the code physically cannot supply a nonce twice, backed by a unique index on (kek_id, nonce); AAD binds tenant/kid/purpose/alg length-prefixed so a moved or relabelled row is undecryptable; schedule periods are bigint seconds not interval, because a month has no fixed length and a grace period must not differ in February. The agent's first concurrency test passed without the lock, so it demoted it to an idempotence test and wrote one that actually fails when the lock is removed. Spec correction accepted and verified against the Final text: key compromise is FAPI 2.0 SP s6.8, not s6.7 (s6.7 is Client Impersonating Resource Owner) - I corrected 2 citations in crates/domain/src/audit and 5 in docs/BACKLOG.md. 381 tests. Runtime wiring is a separate ticket (filed): the binary still uses LocalKeyStore.

TenantKeyStore adapts the tenant-scoped PgKeyRepository to the multi-tenant KeyStore port the router holds, building a repository per call rather than making the repository tenant-agnostic - that would delete the cross-tenant check, which is worth more than an allocation. It lives in store-pg, not server, because it holds a PgPool and the server crate deliberately has no sqlx dependency. KEK source is [keys] kek_file or kek_env, exactly one, no default: a generated-on-boot KEK could not open yesterday's rows and the failure would look like corruption. Startup runs apply_schedule (which creates the first key for a new tenant and applies the schedule for an existing one - same call, so bootstrap cannot diverge from steady state) and then decrypts the active key, so a wrong KEK fails the boot naming both key ids instead of failing the first token. Verified live: kid P3xR_JOb... identical across a restart; missing KEK and both-sources-set each refuse startup; wrong KEK now refuses with 'wrapped under local:wOdO6M1X4TI, this process holds local:qc8QhOcs_aQ'. Also fixed: the redaction scanner classified canonical UUIDs as credentials, which mangled the config path in the startup log. 384 tests.
